events.title: »Flying Sound – Klang. Emotion. Präzision« mit Tigran Maytesian und Daniel Blumenthal
program: Ludwig van Beethoven: Sonate Nr. 5 F-Dur op. 24 »Frühlingssonate«
Franz Schubert: Sonatine Nr. 3 g-Moll D 408
Christoph Willibald Gluck: Melodie (arr. Fritz Kreisler)
Johann Sebastian Bach: Air (arr. August Wilhelmj)
events.intro: Belgian-Armenian violin virtuoso Tigran Maytesian and renowned pianist Daniel Blumenthal perform an evening of chamber music ranging from lyrical intimacy to virtuosic brilliance. The program centers on Beethoven's »Spring Sonata« alongside works by Sarasate, Massenet, Monti, and others, presented in the transparent acoustics of the Kleiner Saal.

events.title: Die Deutsche Kammerphilharmonie Bremen »Haupt­sache Tschai­kowsky« 3. Highlight-Abonnementkonzert
program: Johannes Brahms: Klavierkonzert Nr. 2 B-Dur op. 83
Peter Iljitsch Tschaikowsky: Sinfonie Nr. 4 f-Moll op. 36
events.intro: Pianist Fabian Müller joins the Deutsche Kammerphilharmonie Bremen and conductor Jérémie Rhorer for an evening featuring Brahms's monumental Second Piano Concerto alongside Tchaikovsky's dramatic Fourth Symphony, as part of an ongoing Tchaikovsky project followed by a Scandinavian tour.

events.title: Marc-Uwe Kling: »Neues vom Känguru«
events.intro: Marc-Uwe Kling liest die besten Geschichten aus seinem neuen Buch »Die Känguru-Rebellion«, in dem das Känguru eine Rebellion gegen die Zustände der Welt startet.

events.title: Reiner Calmund »Ein runder Abend – mit Fußball & Freunden«
events.intro: Reiner Calmund, former Bundesliga manager and TV expert, hosts a live football talk show featuring stories, anecdotes, and behind-the-scenes insights from the world of football, joined by a sports moderator and a surprise guest.

events.title: Bremer Kaffeehaus-Orchester »Frisch aufgeblüht« Frühlingskonzert
performers: Klaus Fischer (Flöten, Klarinetten, Saxofon und Moderation)
events.intro: The five musicians celebrate spring with lively Kaffeehaus music featuring melodies by Verdi, Mozart, Ravel and others, alongside swing, tango, jazz and rock. The concert promises virtuosity and playfulness across musical styles and epochs, framed by the ensemble's characteristic witty commentary.
